title: What Did Ancient Humans Actually Do All Night?
description:
It's 6:48 PM, 40,000 years ago. The sun just left, there are no lights, no phone, no door to lock, and something with very big teeth is waking up. So what did ancient humans actually do all night? We spend one Ice Age night with a small band in a river valley in southern France, from sunset to dawn, using what archaeology has found and what studies of modern hunter-gatherers can (and can't) tell us.

Chapters
0:00 A night 40,000 years ago
1:29 6:48 PM - The sun is gone
2:11 7:20 PM - The fire wakes up
2:57 8:30 PM - Story time
4:21 9:40 PM - Hands stay busy
6:03 10:15 PM - The bed
7:26 12:40 AM - The night shift
8:22 2:40 AM - The second sleep?
8:59 3:14 AM - The hour of the hyena
10:18 5:10 AM - The coldest hour
10:40 6:30 AM - Dawn

This is a dramatized reconstruction. The people, camp and night scenes are AI-generated visuals (not real footage of the past); archaeological sites, artifacts and nature shots are real footage/photos credited below. Studies of modern hunter-gatherers (Ju/'hoansi, Hadza, San, Tsimane) are used as clues, not as a time machine.
